tellings.difference: Puts it in the 1980s and says every president had to attend.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of Doug Coe, a leader of the Family, holding prayer breakfasts in Washington.

plain: Powerful people in Washington are said to gather at prayer breakfasts, meetings where officials pray and talk together, and a man named Doug Coe is said to have been behind them. Michels tells it himself, without naming a source. He says Coe was one of the leaders of a group called the Family in the 1980s, and that every president had to attend his prayer breakfast. Peter Levenda, a researcher billed as a CIA historian, also brings it up without a source: "they had prayer breakfasts and that kind of thing," he says, and they get together and talk, and he names Coe. It is told as a sign that a quiet private network had a way into the highest offices in the country.
